menuNote: Le Becco dell'Aquila, au-dessus de la vallée de la Sarca
operator: No drop zone: a BASE site, the most jumped exit in the world. The Italian BASE Association keeps the rules (a deployment line for one-piece and wingsuit pilots, ropes on the way down to the exit) and a windsock on the landing field, seen from the exit.

base.name: Becco dell'Aquila
base.evidence: The Italian BASE Association: the Becco dell'Aquila, a natural platform 15 m by 5 m lightly inclined toward the Sarca valley, 1200 m of elevation, the landing field's windsock in sight. OSM puts a node named Becco dell'Aquila in the woods at 45.99385, 10.90442, 1320 m in the LiDAR, with no drop in front of it; Google Maps has a 'Brento BASE Exit' about 45.99527, 10.90547, at the foot of the wall in the LiDAR, 70 m east of its rim, as a pin set on a satellite picture of a cliff would be. On the rim at that latitude the 1 m LiDAR has a buttress 300 m down, a few metres out, and a slope of 27 degrees behind; 15 m north of it the rim makes a small spur, flat for 10 m behind its lip at 1400 m, falling 380 m within 8 m and 430 m within 20 m, clear of the buttress, 1185 m above the field. The run starts 9 m back from that lip, heading 90 (east), square to the wall; the field is 1.7 km out at 100.

wind.description: The Ora del Garda blows up the valley from the lake, from the south, from late morning, and grows strong by midday: jumps are made early in the morning and late in the afternoon. The Pelèr, from the north, can blow in the morning.

invented: Exit position: the Becco's coordinates are not published and OSM's node has no drop in front of it; the spot used here is the flat spur on the rim nearest to the 'Brento BASE Exit' of Google Maps, chosen in the 1 m LiDAR.
Pattern: inferred from the shape of the valley and the field.
